infl_ens.data.benchmarks.base¶

Common interface for AI-safety benchmark adapters.

Each benchmark module under infl_ens.data.benchmarks provides a loader that returns a BenchmarkSplit: a uniform container of (prompt, score) records plus benchmark-level metadata. The score is the benchmark’s axis in the influencer-game trait space:

  • infl_ens.data.benchmarks.beavertails → harm score in [0, 1], where 1 means “the response is harmful”. The trait-space axis is “harmfulness of prompts the agent serves”.

  • infl_ens.data.benchmarks.halueval → hallucination score in [0, 1], where 1 means “the response contains hallucinations”.

The combined two-axis trait space is built by infl_ens.data.benchmarks.safety_trait_space.build_safety_trait_space().

Classes

BenchmarkSplit(name, prompts, scores, axis_name)

A loaded benchmark split in a single uniform shape.
class infl_ens.data.benchmarks.base.BenchmarkSplit(name, prompts, scores, axis_name, responses=<factory>, metadata=<factory>)[source]¶

Bases: object

A loaded benchmark split in a single uniform shape.

Parameters:

  • name (str) – Benchmark identifier (e.g. 'beavertails', 'halueval-qa').

  • prompts (list[str]) – Raw user-facing prompts, length N. These are what the trait-space encoder will embed.

  • scores (numpy.ndarray) – Per-prompt benchmark axis score in [0, 1], length N. Higher means “more of the property the benchmark measures” (e.g. more harmful, more hallucinated).

  • responses (list[str]) – Optional per-prompt response strings (used at SFT time). Length N or empty.

  • axis_name (str) – Human-readable axis name, e.g. 'harm' or 'hallucination'.

  • metadata (dict) – Free-form metadata (split name, version, source URL).
